title: smbench
summary: Benchmarks for selective agent memory: memory systems compared under one fixed protocol, so the memory system is the only thing that varies.

protocol.label: Embedder
protocol.value: BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5, local, the same for every system

protocol.label: Retrieval depth
protocol.value: k = 20 memories per question, one retrieval, one answer

protocol.label: Answer prompt
protocol.value: One shared prompt for every system (benchmark/src/smbench/locomo/prompts.py)

protocol.label: Load on ALCF
protocol.value: At most 6 concurrent requests, enforced by the local gateway

protocol.label: Accuracy
protocol.value: LLM-judge accuracy with 95% Wilson intervals; paired systems compared with an exact McNemar test

systems.name: Hindsight
systems.notes: Best fit for selective memory: label-set IDs as tags through a validator hook, observations keep their sources. Adapter waits for consolidation before questions.

systems.name: Mem0
systems.notes: Adapter fixes needed for a fair run: max_tokens raised to 8000 (default cut extraction off), and extraction dated to the session (OSS uses today's date).

systems.name: Falda
systems.notes: Rob Ross's fork. Strongest lineage (atoms link to source turns); physical per-store isolation.

systems.name: AWS AgentCore Memory
systems.notes: Reference backend only. Self-managed extraction strategy keeps the model fixed.

benchmarks.name: LoCoMo
benchmarks.measures: Recall over long two-person conversations: 10 conversations, 272 sessions, 1,540 questions (adversarial excluded).
benchmarks.note: Category names follow the data (category 1 averages 3.1 evidence turns). The Mem0 and Hindsight papers call category 1 "single-hop" and 4 "open-domain"; published comparisons are aligned by number.

benchmarks.name: Selective memory
benchmarks.measures: Leaks of locked memory, retelling, permitted recall and side effects in generated multi-agent worlds, with Cedar as the answer key.

benchmarks.name: LongMemEval
benchmarks.measures: Long-term chat memory across 500 questions; a subset first.

benchmarks.name: Speed
benchmarks.measures: Cedar evaluation, filtered vector search, AgentCore fan-out, complex-policy stress.

runs.tokens: Memory systems 10.1M prompt + 2.6M completion (both); answers and judging ~2M per system
runs.conclusion: Tied: Hindsight 69.5% vs Mem0 69.4% (paired p = 0.96). Efficacy does not separate these two systems.
Hindsight 70.4% vs Mem0 61.2% (p = 0.04) on one conversation; not borne out by the full run.

published.setup: gpt-oss-120b, answered via reflect, gpt-oss-120b judge
Platform v3, top-200 retrieval (~7k tokens per query), models not stated

findings.text: Hindsight and Mem0 are tied on full LoCoMo under a fixed protocol; the 9-point pilot gap was single-conversation noise.
Runs of the same conversation vary by about ±5 points, so claims need all questions and ideally repeated runs.

Our Mem0 result matches its paper (69.4% vs 66.9%). Our Hindsight result is 16 points below its paper on the same model; the likely causes are reflect-based answering, retrieval budget and a same-model judge.
Mem0's default max_tokens silently dropped every extraction on full sessions; its open-source add() dated memories to today. Both fixed in the adapter.
Hindsight adapter answered before consolidation finished on some conversations. Fixed; re-running the questions changed accuracy by 0.1 points.
